new_description:
tdf#168604 svx: respect disabled text wrapping in custom shapes

This fixes a regression introduced by
commit 620b89adea77519fd5d057cac7e1acf8a6fb2544
(tdf#165321: fix missing shapes or shapes with near-zero height).

Text in imported PowerPoint custom shapes can wrap onto multiple
lines even when word wrapping is disabled.

Honor the wrapping setting for custom shapes, including when text
autofit is enabled. Keep the existing behavior for other text frames.

Add a test to check that rotated text stays on one line when wrapping
is disabled, whether aligned left, center or right. Also check that
text still wraps when wrapping is enabled, and repeat the layout
checks after enabling text autofit and after saving and reopening
the presentation as PPTX.

AI assistance was used to develop the implementation and regression
test, analyze the issue, and prepare the Gerrit submission.

new_description:
tdf#168604 svx: honor no-wrap and overflow alignment in custom shapes

For custom shapes, CustomShapeProperties::UpdateTextFrameStatus maps
resize-shape-to-fit-text to mbTextFrame via SDRATTR_TEXT_AUTOGROWHEIGHT.
Using IsTextFrame() to force a width constraint therefore wraps text
even when the custom shape explicitly disables wrapping.

In block-text decomposition, retain forced wrapping for real text
frames but let custom shapes honor their word-wrap setting. Preserve
the existing cell and unlimited-page handling.

Allow the existing BLOCK-to-paragraph-alignment correction to run for
non-wrapping custom shapes that report text-frame status. Apply the
corresponding correction in SdrObjCustomShape::TakeTextRect so rendered
overflow and calculated text rectangles have consistent anchoring.
Without these corrections, the no-wrap-only fix leaves centered text
misplaced.

Do not enlarge the stored shape rectangle or revert the transformed
geometry preservation from tdf#165321. Leave shrink-to-fit decomposition
unchanged: spAutoFit resizes the shape, unlike normAutofit, which shrinks
the text.

Add a sanitized regression with left/center/right no-wrap shapes,
wrap-enabled and non-growing controls, and a shape in a scaled group.
Check per-object primitives, overflow alignment, TakeTextRect, rotation,
size, centers, geometry preservation and PPTX reload. Verify real text
frames still wrap.

AI assistance was used for implementation, investigation and testing.
Local validation used isolated builds with existing dependencies on
AlmaLinux 9/WSL1 GCC and native Windows MSVC. Each passed 62 import,
24 layout and 76 OOXML export tests. The new regression fails against
the earlier renderer on both platforms. These runs are not a clean
current-master full build or an original-presentation GUI validation.

The regression is formatted with the repository-pinned clang-format
5.0.0. Fresh standard CI is required for this rebased revision.

After switching off bold, italic or underline at the end of a line,

latest user choice and has to be respected, so it now overrides the
previously copied ending one.

libX11 is now not required when building with GTK 3 without X11 support

new_description:
tdf#146153 Don't check for legacy libGL

libGL supports OpenGL and GLX and may not be present when libglvnd is
installed.

Only libepoxy is directly used. N.B. because of b8838667e495
("tdf#146153 gtk: Don't include gen/x11-specific unx/saldisp.hxx",
2026-10-23) epoxy/glx.h is only included when building the gen/x11 vcl
plugin.

Require libepoxy for OpenGL support instead.

old_description:
tdf#146153 Enable building the GUI --without-x

Added a new variable, using_unix_desktop, in configure.ac that
controls features that are currently controlled by using_x11 but are not
unique to X11. A matching output variable and C preprocessor macro are
created.

The default value is set per platform and it is always set to false when
the user passes --disable-gui.

gtktiledviewer is not built with --without-x.

libICE, libSM, libXext, libXinerama and libXrender are no longer used.

libX11 and epoxy/glx are still required.

libXt is required when Java support is enabled.

Removes an attempt to open an X11 display on application startup.

old_description:
tdf#126008 sw: preserve table border overrides across row edits

AI generated patch description: "
Writer reapplies a table style after row edits. The refresh added in change
190027 respects a cell's direct-format marker, but SetTabBorders does not set
that marker, and ODF does not store it. In the attached document, deleting the
'Ethernet driver' row therefore restores separators that the user removed.

Track directly set border lines and padding distances per side. SetTabBorders
marks each requested side, including a value that currently equals the style;
simple ODF table import reconstructs differences from the resolved positional
style. Style refresh merges only marked sides into the new style box, allowing
unmarked borders, background, and text formatting to update. Carry the direct
markers through box copy, insertion, and undo, and clear a copied line marker
when a structural edit deliberately removes that edge. Release temporary
parent styles while resolving inherited table styles for the import scan.

The regression uses the public tdf#126008 document. It checks row deletion,
style-controlled borders and background, border-only insertion and copy,
same-value setters, padding, whole-cell direct formatting, and undo. Complex
nested tables are outside the import comparison because their style positions
require a different traversal.
"

Assisted-by: GPT 6.1 Sol High

tdf#161592: check grouped formulas after interpretation

InterpretCellsIfNeeded() checks each grouped cell immediately after queueing it, before CellInterpreterBase flushes the group. Flush the pending group before returning and check its members after interpretation. Ungrouped formulas retain their immediate check, and the ordinary dirty-cell path has no added status checks.

old_description:
tdf#170671 sw: track copied header/footer sections through undo

The report bibisects the modern paste/undo regression to
68e1db614c8618f0155d157cb1dc4c6f259b8573 (Gerrit 185940), which added
section undo for copied headers and footers to fix tdf#148703.

Removing pasted body fly content shifts later header/footer sections.
The saved numeric offsets then identify unrelated nodes, and SaveSection
can access past the end of the document. Retain a SwNodeIndex instead
and refresh it through RestoreSection when redoing the paste.

CopyFlyInFlyImpl also records standalone fly undo actions inside these
sections. SaveSection already saves their anchored objects in its history,
so the standalone actions later operate on deleted formats. Use the
existing destination UndoGuard for the nested fly copy, and restore the
section history on redo, as footnote and redline section undo already do.

Keep the page-style naming and stashed-format lookup from
f89ca556d475f1013aa77a6c78034c9c417ea463 (Gerrit 207604). The existing
tdf#148703 and tdf#171068 regressions still pass.

Add the original attachment regression and a smaller generated footer-frame
case. Both fail with original runtime code; the fixed tests check repeated
undo/redo, node/object counts, exact body text and nested footer-frame text.
Validated the original application workflow and sw_core_undo (15),
sw_core_doc (50) and sw_uiwriter8 (84) on macOS arm64.

https://gerrit.libreoffice.org/c/core/+/185940

tdf#151958: cache exact COUNTIF string counts safely

AI generated patch description: "Commit 5b189abc13d4 let COUNTIF use a collator-sorted range cache. Its binary search can disagree with COUNTIF's whole-cell shared-string equality, especially when date-formatted numbers and text share a range. Re-enabling that path returns 5 and 82 on the reported document where direct evaluation returns 17 and 6. Commit 9a555d79b3b0 therefore disabled the sorted-cache path for COUNTIF and COUNTIFS.

For nonempty whole-cell string equality, build a distinct count cache using the same formatted shared strings and case folding as direct COUNTIF. Keep numeric, wildcard, relational, and COUNTIFS queries on their current direct paths. Above 65,536 distinct strings, fall back to direct evaluation without retaining the large count map.

Invalidate exact counts when source values, formats, styles, document options, or bulk-import attribute runs can change their strings. Iterate populated cells in sparse ranges while listening to the original range. Tests cover the reported fixture, case and Unicode behavior, format and style edits, null-date and bulk-import changes, sparse columns, and the distinct-string limit. A replay of both reported documents returned the expected counts. The style-edit path depends on change 212785."

old_description:
vcl: unify Region transformations in outdev map.cxx

This commit eliminates duplicated routing logic between
OutputDevice::LogicToPixel(const vcl::Region&) and
OutputDevice::PixelToLogic(const vcl::Region&).

The identical data-structure traversal (handling B2DPolyPolygon,
PolyPolygon, and RegionBand) has been extracted into a generic
template helper lcl_TransformRegion().

Technical details:
- Used a C++14 generic lambda (const auto& obj) to let the compiler
automatically resolve the correct LogicToPixel/PixelToLogic overload.
- Removed a legacy C++98 const_reverse_iterator workaround during
the RegionBand RectangleVector traversal, taking advantage of modern
auto type deduction.
new_description:
vcl: clarify CoordinateMapper offsets and unify Region transforms

This commit addresses two distinct cleanups in the VCL mapping logic:

1. Coordinate Offset Renaming:
Ambiguous offset variables and their associated getters/setters in
CoordinateMapper have been renamed to explicitly describe the coordinate
spaces they transition between:
- mnOutOffX/Y -> mnDeviceToWindowOffsetX/Y
- mnOutOffOrigX/Y -> mnWindowToViewOffsetX/Y
- mnOutOffLogicX/Y -> mnLogicToAbsoluteOffsetX/Y
Associated methods (e.g., GetPixelOffset -> GetWindowToViewOffset,
WindowToLogicSubPixel -> WindowToViewSubPixel) were updated to match
this clearer nomenclature.

2. Region Transformation Unification:
Eliminates duplicated routing logic between OutputDevice::LogicToPixel
and PixelToLogic for vcl::Region. The identical data-structure traversal
(handling B2DPolyPolygon, PolyPolygon, and RegionBand) is extracted into
a generic lcl_TransformRegion() template helper. This utilizes a C++14
generic lambda to resolve the correct overload and modernizes the
RectangleVector traversal.

new_description:
jvmfwk: add SunVersion test for individual version parts

Instead of simply assuming version parsing works because comparing
two versions comes out the right way, actually make sure the code
parses the versions as we expect.

old_description:
tdf#174161: fix Java version detection for 5-component versions

Newer versions like "27.0.1.2.3" fail to parse becuase the existing
code only allows 4 version components. The existing code also does
a bunch of open-coded string manipulation. Replace that code with
a comphelper::string::split()-based approach for the easy parts.

For the last, more complicated component that may contain multiple
version sub-components and alpha-numberic parts, switch to a more
procedural method (rather than loop-based) as this last component
can be parsed lexigraphically.

Finally, un-#ifdef the FreeBSD code as there's no reason it needs
to be FreeBSD-specific. Add a testcase for it too.
new_description:
tdf#174161: fix Java version detection for 5-component versions

Newer versions like "27.0.1.2.3" fail to parse becuase the existing
code only allows 4 version components. The existing code also does
a bunch of open-coded string manipulation. Replace that code with
a split()-based approach for the easy parts. Unfortunately we must
copy most of the comphelper::string::split() code into jvmfwk
because linking to comphelper here creates a circular dependency
for --enable-mergelib. Thankfully it's small.

For the last, more complicated component that may contain multiple
version sub-components and alpha-numberic parts, switch to a more
procedural method (rather than loop-based) as this last component
can be parsed lexigraphically.

Finally, un-#ifdef the FreeBSD code as there's no reason it needs
to be FreeBSD-specific. Add a testcase for it too.

old_description:
tdf#171849 DOCX import: prefer direct list indent over style fallback

When a paragraph disables an inherited character-based indent with
w:leftChars="0", the importer copies the paragraph style's twip-based
left margin as a fallback. This overrides the indentation of directly
applied numbering and shifts the list text to the right.

Use the direct numbering's IndentAt instead, and retain its first-line
indent when materializing the left margin. Explicit paragraph indentation
still takes precedence. Keep the existing fallback for paragraphs without
direct numbering.

Add a reduced reproducer covering list indentation, explicit left and
first-line indentation, and the fallback without numbering, on import
and DOCX save/reload.

AI assistance was used for code analysis, implementation, regression-test
preparation, Windows and Linux validation, and submission preparation.
new_description:
tdf#171849 DOCX import: resolve numbering indents before style fallback

When a paragraph disables an inherited character-based indent, the
importer resolves its twip-based fallback without considering numbering.
This can copy an older paragraph-style indent into direct formatting,
overriding the numbering and shifting the list text to the right.

Resolve left and first-line numbering indents in GetAnyProperty instead
of handling the left indent locally in DomainMapper. Preserve explicit
paragraph indentation. For numbering inherited through a style, preserve
indents on that style and on derived styles, while resolving numbering
before indentation from older base styles.

Use the effective numbering level and distinguish a zero indent from an
absent property. Do not copy the first-line indent as a side effect of
resolving the left indent.

This follows Word-compatible import behavior. MS-OI29500 sections
2.1.229 and 2.1.44(a) document Word's numbering/style ordering and its
treatment of zero character-unit indents. The inherited-style cases were
also checked independently in Microsoft Word.

Expand the reproducer to cover direct and inherited numbering, explicit
and zero indents, style boundaries, effective levels, disabled numbering,
attribute order, and preservation of numbering on import and DOCX
save/reload.

AI assistance was used for code analysis, implementation, regression-test
preparation, standards research, Windows and Linux validation, and
submission preparation.

old_description:
sr: spelling corrections from serbian-dictionaries 1.1

Port the corrections of serbian-dictionaries 1.1
(https://github.com/sociolog/serbian-dictionaries, corrections.tsv, where
each is listed with its source) to sr.dic and sr-Latn.dic.

Each correction is matched by the word forms it gives, not by its
flags:

- 147 entries are taken out. 12 of them also gave correct forms, which
stay through narrower entries (сип/1125 gave сипски; it is now сип).
- 356 entries are added, all with LibreOffice's own affix classes.
The 90 capitalised place names of 1.0.1 are left out: LibreOffice
already accepts them through its lowercase entries.
- One affix rule had a Latin o in a Cyrillic ending (SFX 448 ац цoм,
as in Барајевцoм); it is now Cyrillic. Two entries had a Latin
letter (корејa, папратиштe).

No longer accepted: forms the Pravopis doesn't accept (кљешта, гњездо,
раздјел, мршавети, long-stem comparatives such as лијепши), dictionary
errors (онјлајн, понједељак), spellings with њ for нј in Cyrillic
(коњугација), and misspelled words found in a review of rare
words (изашто, сипски, раденик, објезбеђење, изказати, монофизтски,
унитаризција, америћки).

Now accepted: missing words (бијел, цијел, рјеђи, итекако, вебсајт,
лејди, сријемски), ijekavian twins of ekavian words, and standard words
from the Rečnik srpskoga jezika headwords (динозаур, егида, љубица).

Suggestions: the KEY line of both files had a Latin s among the keys
(sџцвбнм, sdžcvbnm); it is removed. MAP, TRY and REP tables are added,
so racunar offers računar first, skola offers škola and djak offers đak.

Checked by expanding every entry in both files: a form's verdict
changes only where a correction touches it, and there it matches
serbian-dictionaries 1.1 (12,359 Cyrillic and 9,939 Latin forms and
their capitalised forms). Hunspell 1.7 gives the same verdicts, also in
upper case, and the same as before on a random sample of 100,000 other
forms.

Made with tools/port_libreoffice.py of that repository (640deda);
tools/check_libreoffice.py repeats these checks.

old_description:
tdf#173028 sw: detach remembered search attributes from document pools

Writer retains search and replacement attribute lists across documents.
Since 2984dd49fb9fb2f8d3d56fba0db34a7b95666ce1 (Gerrit 165167),
SearchAttrItemList copies SfxPoolItemHolders which keep a raw pointer to
the original document's pool. Closing that document leaves the remembered
list dangling; opening Find & Replace in another document crashes while
clearing it.

https://gerrit.libreoffice.org/c/core/+/165167

Give copied lists an owned clone of their source pool and bind their
holders to it. This reuses SfxItemPool::Clone, retaining attribute and
format criteria without keeping the original SwAttrPool/SwDoc alive.
Move the owned pool together with its holders and clear holders before
releasing the pool. Explicitly release Writer's remembered lists during
SwDLL shutdown, before removing its item-info packages.

The UI regressions retain each of the first three attribute criteria,
and a concrete underline format, across closing and reopening Writer
documents. The attribute regression crashes without the fix. Both cases
pass with the fix and the application exits cleanly; the complete
Find & Replace UI suite passes all 17 tests.

old_description:
tdf#170520 vcl: split disabled text color from disabled color

The two UI color settings 'Disabled color' and 'Disabled text color'
were cross-wired in practice. All code paths that render disabled text
were reading StyleSettings::GetDisableColor() (the 'Disabled color'
setting), while the 'Disabled text color' setting was only visible in
the theme color system (ThemeColors::GetDisabledTextColor()) and the
Qt5 palette — but the generic VCL renderer and the GTK3 CSS theme
ignored it entirely for text.

This patch makes the two settings behave as intended:

'Disabled color' -> disabled backgrounds, borders, fills
'Disabled text color' -> disabled text

Changes:

1. Add StyleSettings::GetDisableTextColor() / SetDisableTextColor()
backed by a new maDisableTextColor field (default COL_GRAY).

2. Feed the DISABLEDTEXTCOLOR config value into the new property in
colorcfg.cxx, and fix the COL_AUTO fallback to return the new
property instead of shadow color.

3. Switch every SetTextColor() / set_font_color() / text-color
assignment that was using GetDisableColor() to the new
GetDisableTextColor() (19 sites across vcl, sfx2, sc, svx,
dbaccess, desktop, chart2, svtools).

4. Fix GTK3 custom-theme.cxx so the disabled treeview expander text
uses GetDisabledTextColor() instead of GetDisabledColor().

Line colors (SetLineColor), fill colors (SetFillColor), frame
brushes, and the UNO WindowStyleSettings API are left on
GetDisableColor() — those are backgrounds/borders, not text.

Qt5 already correctly used ThemeColors::GetDisabledTextColor() for
palette roles; no change needed there.

old_description:
tdf#174332: Properly handle default port for secure connection (443).

When the password for a remote WebDAV server is saved in the
password storage, the default port is removed from the URL.
However the RemoteFilesDialog code looked for the password using
the full URL, including the port.

HostDetailsContainer, which is used indirectly by RemoteFilesDialog,
already handles default port and removes that from the URL. However,
the default port was not set correctly for secure WebDAV connections.

Make sure to set the default port correctly in the code whenever
the WebDAV settings are changed.

old_description:
tdf#59355 read the font table of Publisher 97 files

Publisher 97 character styles already carry a font index, but the font
table (contents chunk type 0x1e) was skipped, so text had no font, and
the 8-bit text was decoded by guessing the code page from the text,
which fails for short texts: the bug document shows "Русский текст..."
as "Ðóññêèé òåêñò...".

Read the font table: the number of fonts at 4, then at 0xe one offset
per font plus an end offset relative to 0xe; an entry is a byte of
unknown use, the pitch and family byte and the 0-terminated name. As
the reporter pointed out, the character set byte is not reliable, but
Windows' script variants name their code page ("Times New Roman Cyr").
If all the fonts used by non-ASCII text are such variants of one script,
use that code page instead of the guess.

The bug document now shows its Russian text in Times New Roman Cyr. The
other sample documents render unchanged.

Fix found with the help of Claude.

old_description:
related tdf#160489 pass font size in points

fo:font-size was inserted as a bare double, i.e. in inches. The ODF
generator writes it with its unit, but pub2xhtml's SVG generator takes
the number as is, so a 33 pt heading became font-size="0.4625" and the
text in the SVG was too small to see.

Insert the size in points, as libvisio and libcdr do. LibreOffice
renders the Apache POI publisher samples and the bug's attachment
pixel-identical before and after; in the SVG the text now has its real
size. Line breaks and alignment inside text boxes are still missing in
the SVG output, that part of the bug is in the SVG generator.

Fix found with the help of Claude.

the number as is, so the 28.7 pt "ADVERTISEMENT HEADING" in the bug's
attachment became font-size="0.3986" and the text in the SVG was too
small to see.

Insert the size in points, as libvisio and libcdr do. LibreOffice
renders the Apache POI publisher samples and the bug's attachment
pixel-identical before and after; in the SVG the text now has its real
size. Line breaks and alignment inside text boxes are still missing in
the SVG output, that part of the bug is in the SVG generator.

libmspub had no unit tests, so this adds a CppUnit setup like
libvisio's (configure --enable-tests, then make check) and one test
that converts fdo59355-1.pub to SVG. That file is a single 10 pt text
box from LibreOffice's writerperfect test data. Without the fix the
test fails with "Expected: 10, Actual: 0.1389". Tests are off by
default because LibreOffice's build of libmspub does not pass
--disable-tests.

Fix and test written with the help of Claude.

old_description:
tdf#174315 cui sw offapi xmloff: split compound words across page

Add loext:hyphenation-split-compound-word to the ODF export/import
to fix DOCX/ODT "do not hyphenate across page" feature for
languages with open compounding, i.e. where splitting compound words
is requested instead of the complete disabling of hyphenation.
new_description:
tdf#174315 cui offapi sw xmloff: split compound words across page

Add optional compound word splitting to the "Do not hyphenate across"
feature (fo:hyphenation-keep). The new Text Flow option and the
associated loext:hyphenation-split-compound-word fix the OpenDocument
and MS-DOCX/CSS4 interoperability feature for languages with open
compounding, i.e. where splitting compound words is requested instead of
the complete disabling of hyphenation because of the frequency of the
closed compound words.

With the new option it's possible to keep MSO/MS-DOCX interoperability,
also introducing a better hyphenation algorithm, which gives better
readability across columns, pages and spreads without bad word spacing
and poor rags, especially in languages like Danish, Dutch, Esperanto,
Estonian, Finnish, German, Hungarian, Icelandic, Latvian, Norwegian and
Swedish (but it can be useful for English etc., too, especially on very
narrow column or page sizes).

Details:

* Add check box in Hyphenate across section on Text Flow pane in
paragraph formatting dialog window;

* Store properties in paragraph model:

css::style::ParagraphProperties::ParaHyphenationSplitCompoundWord

* Add ODF import/export (loext:hyphenation-split-compound-word);

* Add ODF unit tests.

* Fix also the ODF fo:hyphenation-keep implementation by using a
hashCode() based string comparison to update the edited text lines
in column/page/spread end positions immediately.

Follow-up to 698b38a18f5f70fd8d50968bc50951aba7085175
"tdf#165354 sw cui: implement HyphenationKeepLine – part 3",
commit f8b9cd8fd13897094a014ad06df406f0c78adc62

and commit 3e02ffb76c484a05cdc140d8a10bc3d993fe8320
"tdf#i165354 sw offapi DOCX: implement HyphenationKeepLine – part 1".

See also commit e668dc84eb97bf46fc108ec209fc8383a34123f7
"tdf#173389 cui offapi sw xmloff: add custom compound-based
hyphenation".

can be used to display important elements like "Style".

usage of that where it cause that unneeded padding. This patch uses the
second approach.

old_description:
tdf#173310 vcl/RadioButton: Take into account width request

The VCL implementation of radio buttons wasn’t taking into account the
width request when calculating the optimal size. The Macro Security
dialog sets a width request on all of its radio buttons and they all
have text with embedded newlines. If the translation of the text ends up
overflowing the allocated width then the size calculation wasn’t taking
into account the need to wrap the lines when calculating the height and
the text would end up truncated.

This patch makes the implementation of RadioButton::GetOptimalSize be
the same as the one for CheckButton::GetOptimalSize so that the wrapping
will occur.
new_description:
tdf#163552 vcl/RadioButton: Take into account width request

The VCL implementation of radio buttons wasn’t taking into account the
width request when calculating the optimal size. The Macro Security
dialog sets a width request on all of its radio buttons and they all
have text with embedded newlines. If the translation of the text ends up
overflowing the allocated width then the size calculation wasn’t taking
into account the need to wrap the lines when calculating the height and
the text would end up truncated.

This patch makes the implementation of RadioButton::GetOptimalSize be
the same as the one for CheckButton::GetOptimalSize so that the wrapping
will occur.

old_description:
svl: avoid use-after-free on SharedString self-move

Problem:
Move-assigning a SharedString to itself can release its last string
reference. The subsequent pointer exchange restores the freed pointer,
and reading the string can cause a heap-use-after-free.

Fix:
Return immediately for self-move, as copy assignment already does.

Tests:
Add CppUnit coverage for a last-owner string and aliased string data.
CppunitTest_svl_qa_cppunit passes with GCC and Clang compiler plugins
(22 tests each). A standalone ASan/UBSan reproducer detects the bug
before the fix and reads the string safely after the fix.
Full ASan CppUnit and svl.allcheck were not completed locally.

old_description:
gerrit: Excempt Weblate host from Anubis

Weblate does a series of checks to make sure you have configured your
project correctly. One of these checks is BrokenBrowserURL, which uses a
random translation source file to check whether the Git repository
browser works correctly.

On IRC I got a report with the following error:

Client Error: Forbidden for url: https://git.libreoffice.org/core/+/master/shell/inc/spsupp/spsuppStrings.hrc#15

I did a quick curl on the Weblate host to confirm the error and landed
on an Anubis page. This is not necessarily the issue here, since Anubis
responded with HTTP 200. Nevertheless, it's a good idea to excempt
Weblate from Anubus so that we can debug further if necessary.

old_description:
tdf#171093 sc: preserve decimal suffixes in invalid formulas

A leading decimal token directly after a bad name or another number
cannot form a valid expression. Reconstructing it as a double adds a
leading zero, so replacing + with PLUS in French =1+2,5 produces
=1plus20,5. English =11.3.5 similarly becomes =11.30.5.

Keep that adjacent decimal suffix as an invalid string token with its
original spelling. RPN compilation still reports OperatorExpected.
Numbers after operators, whitespace boundaries and inline arrays
retain their existing handling.

Add English, French and German coverage for formula reconstruction,
reparsing, trailing-zero and repeated suffixes, and valid decimals.

Assisted by GPT 6.1 Sol High
new_description:
tdf#171093 sc: preserve decimal suffixes in invalid formulas

Reconstructing an adjacent decimal suffix as a double adds a leading
zero, so replacing + with PLUS in French =1+2,5 produces =1plus20,5.
English =11.3.5 similarly becomes =11.30.5. The same problem occurs
after references, strings, closing parentheses and postfix operators.

Keep a decimal suffix as an invalid string token when its predecessor
does not admit another operand. Preserve the preceding number too when
another decimal suffix follows: normalizing =1.2e3.5 to =1200.5 otherwise
turns an invalid expression into a valid number on reparsing. Retain
invalid inline-array contents without merging them into a matrix.
RPN/array compilation continues to report the appropriate syntax error.

Numbers after operators, argument/array separators and whitespace
retain their ordinary handling. Add English, French and German coverage
for reconstruction and reparsing, all preceding operand categories,
exponents, repeated suffixes, invalid arrays and valid decimal controls.

old_description:
Related tdf#148576: Fix GetZipStorageToSign_Impl error in logs

When opening a password-protected XLSX document, the console reported:
GetZipStorageToSign_Impl: failed to create ZIP storage

For the remind, an non encrypted xlsx is a zip with a specific structure. An encrypted xlsx isn't a encrypted zip but a CFB (Compound File Binary)
which begins with D0 CF 11 E0.

The signature verification code attempted to create a ZIP storage from the original input stream,
which contains an OLE compound file (D0 CF 11 E0) rather than a ZIP package.
OOXML decryption is handled by oox/source/core/filterdetect.cxx and the decrypted package stream is stored
in the MediaDescriptor's ComponentData under the DecryptedPackage key. The pb is SfxMedium::GetZipStorageToSign_Impl() did not use it.

Retrieve the decrypted package stream from ComponentData and use it to create the ZIP storage when available.
Keep the existing input stream as a fallback for non-encrypted documents.
This allows signature-related operations to access the actual decrypted OOXML package without modifying the existing OOXML decryption or ODF encryption mechanisms.

I tested this with the password-protected XLSX document from tdf#148576.
The document opens successfully and the error log doesn't appear again.

tdf#174076 sw: allow all use of table styles for insert/convert

This fixes a long-standing UI failure.

Only the built-in table styles were being made available
for use when inserting a table, or converting text to table.

It was missing table styles that were imported with the document.

Ideally we could just use GetDoc()->GetTableStyles()

We probably could, but I just can't be confident that
in every conceivable case the rView.GetWrtShell().GetDoc() SwDoc*
will never be null.
So we add more wastefulness by copying it instead.

old_description:
filter: optional JSON export report for PDF conversions

Add PDFWriter::GetEmbeddedFontNames (forwarding to
PDFWriterImpl::getEmbeddedFontNames over the subset, Type3 and
system font maps), and an env-gated export report: when
LO_PDF_EXPORT_REPORT is set to a value other than "" or "0",
PDFExport prepares a JSON report after a successful export with
the facts the filter and writer know directly -- page count, PDF
version, tagged and PDF/UA flags, the SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH in
effect, and the embedded font family names -- and PDFFilter
writes it as <output>.report.json next to the exported PDF.

PDFExport renders into a temporary file and PDFFilter streams
the result to the descriptor's output stream, so the final
output path is only known in PDFFilter: the report carries a
placeholder that PDFFilter replaces with the descriptor's file
path before writing the sidecar. Stream-only targets (no file
URL in the descriptor) get no sidecar.

The document's requested font names are not known at the export
layer, so substitution pairs are deliberately not reported.

Also export PDFWriter::GetSourceDateEpoch (VCL_DLLPUBLIC): the
report is its first caller outside libvcl.

Developed with an AI assistant (Árbol, running Muse); the human submitter has reviewed the changes and the test evidence.

old_description:
tdf#174099 sw: don't ask a blank portion for a trailing hole portion

Since commit e3c068cb190e6cf04a49f9984f984d5ef72f9d9a (tdf#167946:
reimplement the fix for tdf#120677, 2026-02-07), SwBlankPortion formats
via SwTextPortion::Format, so an NBSP goes through SwTextGuess::Guess.
When the NBSP is followed by blanks up to the paragraph end (or a line
break), maybeAdjustPositionsForBlockAdjust asks for a trailing
SwHolePortion by returning false. But SwTextPortion::Format_ creates
that hole, and resets bFull, only for portions outside InExpGrp, and
PortionType::Blank is in it. So the portion stayed "full", and
SwBlankPortion::Format underflowed the preceding word to the next line,
block-adjusting the previous line as if it weren't the last.

Exempt blank portions, as field portions already are: a one-character
NBSP portion has no trailing blanks of its own; the following blanks
are in the next text portion.
new_description:
tdf#174099 sw: let a blank portion carry a trailing hole portion

Since commit e3c068cb190e6cf04a49f9984f984d5ef72f9d9a (tdf#167946:
reimplement the fix for tdf#120677, 2026-02-07), SwBlankPortion is an
SwTextPortion and formats via SwTextPortion::Format, so an NBSP goes
through SwTextGuess::Guess. When only blanks follow the NBSP up to the
paragraph end (or a line break), maybeAdjustPositionsForBlockAdjust
asks for a trailing SwHolePortion by returning false. But
SwTextPortion::Format_ creates that hole, and resets bFull, only for
portions outside InExpGrp, and PortionType::Blank is still in that
group from when SwBlankPortion was an SwExpandPortion. So the portion
stayed "full", and SwBlankPortion::Format underflowed the preceding
word to the next line, block-adjusting the previous line as if it
weren't the last.

Create the hole for blank portions too, except for a field's hook char,
which has no length and is formatted from the field's expansion.

old_description:
vcl: honour SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH in PDF export

PDFWriter::GetDateTime and vcl::pdf::computeDocumentIdentifier read
the system time directly, so every PDF export differed from the
previous one in the info-dict CreationDate, the XMP dates, the
trailer /ID (whose digest hashes the raw time value) and the
/DocChecksum.

Add PDFWriter::GetSourceDateEpoch, which parses the SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
environment variable as a non-negative integer of seconds since
1970-01-01 UTC. When it is set, both call sites use the epoch instead
of the system time and format it in UTC; a signing context that
carries its own signature time keeps precedence. With the variable
unset or invalid, behaviour is unchanged.

Two conversions of the same document with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH set now
produce byte-identical PDFs.

Developed with an AI assistant (Árbol, running Muse); the human submitter has reviewed the changes and the test evidence.

old_description:
tdf#173780 vcl: put content inside an artifact into its marked content

The text of a decorative shape begins a Paragraph inside the shape's
NonStructElement. beginStructureElementMCSeq opened /Artifact only for
the NonStructElement itself, so the text was in no marked content at
all (PDF/UA-1 7.1-3). Open the artifact on the nearest NonStructElement
ancestor instead, and keep it open until that element ends, so the
whole shape is one artifact; leaving the element otherwise, by
setCurrentStructureElement or at the page end, still closes it.

all (PDF/UA-1 7.1-3). Open the artifact on the nearest NonStructElement
ancestor instead, and keep it open until that element ends, so the
whole shape is one artifact; leaving the element otherwise, by
setCurrentStructureElement or at the page end, still closes it.

Text with character transparency is drawn into a transparency group, so
the marked content began inside the group's form XObject and ended in
the page stream. Begin it in beginTransparencyGroup, before redirecting,
so that it contains the group. This also happened before with a normal
text box.

new_description:
tdf#174233 sw: use InsertOrReplaceAutoFormat when cancelling

This fixes a 26.8 regression
from commit 513bfbd476113f648090a8275cece4dc04ba0463.

This patch depends on the new InsertOrReplaceAutoFormat function
that was introduced for tdf#174076.

It was deleting the table style and then re-adding it.
That ends up being very bad because it removes it as a parent style,
and then the styles get assigned to a somewhat random parent.

old_description:
tdf#94113 sw a11y: Set and report the caret in the correct frame

This fixes tdf#94113 ("Accessible focus event missing when caret moves
to start of paragraph spanning two pages"), and covers other problematic
cases: ATs setting the caret position to paragraphs laid out in multiple
frames (paragraphs spanning multiple pages, page headers, footers,
repeated table headings) could move it to the first paragraph instance
instead of the requested one. See [1] ("Jumping forward in LibreOffice
Writer document jumps back to the first instance of repeated elements")

This was caused by resolving the caret position without accounting for
the frame in which the accessibility object was present. This meant
multiple instances of that accessibility node claimed the caret was in
them, hence the first fragment never reported losing the caret.

SwAccessibleParagraph now accounts for the frame the cursor is in when
reporting the caret position and its FOCUSED state, so that (hopefully)
only one object reports it at once.

scaffolding, feedback and part of test generation.

old_description:
sal: prevent stack overflow with negative decimal precision

Problem:
The SAL double-to-string formatter estimates its temporary stack buffer
from nDigits, the number of digits retained after rounding. When fixed-point
formatting uses negative decimal precision, nDigits can be zero or negative
even though the formatter still writes the full integer part and its group
separators. The buffer can therefore be smaller than the generated output.

For example, formatting 1e20 with precision -15 and no grouping overflows
the buffer. Formatting 1e14 with precision -15 and grouping {1, 0} also
overflows it. Both cases are confirmed by AddressSanitizer.

Fix:
Size the buffer from the complete integer width after rounding, plus any
fractional digits, the maximum number of group separators, and space for
the sign, decimal point and exponent. This prevents the out-of-bounds
writes without changing rounding or the generated text.

Add a CppUnit regression test for both original reproductions and other
negative-precision boundaries, covering UTF-16 and byte strings, both
signs, trailing-zero settings, grouped output, and rounding carry.

Tested with sal.allcheck on Linux ARM64: 1610 tests pass under GCC dbgutil
and Clang ASan/UBSan. Leak detection was disabled for the CppUnit runner's
existing intentional retained allocations; ASan memory-access checks and
UBSan remained enabled.

Note:
The original grouped reproducer also exposes a pre-existing formatting
issue: rounding 1e14 to 10^15 with grouping {1, 0} produces a leading group
separator. That behavior is outside the scope of this memory-safety fix
and will be addressed separately. The regression test exercises the exact
crashing input but deliberately does not assert the malformed output as
the expected string.

old_description:
core: Remove FSCKFIX setting

The setting is handled by the "initscripts" package, which no longer
exists on newer systems.

Instead of introducing a bunch of workarounds, I decided to dig a
little to see whether this is needed.

Newer systemd has a systemd-fsck@.service which recognises a fsck.repair
variable on the kernel command line. We could patch up
GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT to include fsck.repair=yes, but here is the
section on fsck.repair from systemd-fsck@.service(8):

> fsck.repair=
> One of "preen", "yes", "no". Controls the mode of operation. The
> default is "preen", and will automatically repair problems that can
> be safely fixed. "yes" will answer yes to all questions by fsck and
> "no" will answer no to all questions.
>
> Added in version 213.

So the default is already what we want to have, because if repair
results in data loss, we certainly want to investigate manually.

Since all our machines run systemd, and the first systemd with that
behaviour was version 12, I think it's safe to just remove the setting.

Here is the systemd commit that introduced fsck wrappers:

https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/3d20ed6d51e38968cd646e2b3b24f36673408024

Note that the "-a" option is responsible for auto-repair, the "preen"
opton was just added later so you could change away from the default
behaviour.

old_description:
Recognize localized font typographic family names

This relates to tdf#63011, which was indirectly and partially fixed by
https://gerrit.libreoffice.org/c/core/+/207742. That patch and the
patches linked to tdf#172647 allow the program to find the correct font
when a document requests a font that is embedded but not installed on
the system. However, those patches only load Font Family names (ID 1) as
aliases, so the font cannot be found if the document requests a
non-default Typographic Family name (ID 16). Such documents can be
generated by the latest version of LibreOffice (but not currently by MS
Office). Source Han Sans is one example of a font with multiple
Typographic Family names in different languages.

To solve this problem, match against all Typographic Family names first,
and then fall back to Font Family names if the requested font is not
found among the loaded Typographic Family names.

Retain `bAbortOnFontSubstitute` to guard the steps that enumerate all
names for ID 1 or ID 16. The purpose is to make testing faster.

Update `TestFontFace` with binary `OpenType` name tables containing
multilingual records, and add unit tests to verify alias resolution for
ID 1 and ID 16.

AI Disclosure: AI was used to implement all the code in this patch under
the author's direction. The author chose the fallback mechanism, the
approach to mocking in tests, and the data structure.

old_description:
tdf#92375 xmloff: persist assumed PNG size on ODF export

Physical crop distances use a graphic's intrinsic size. When a PNG has
no resolution, that size depends on display DPI. Copying its native
bytes unchanged on save loses the author's assumption, so reopening
the ODF on a different display changes the crop.

Persist the effective physical preferred size as PNG pHYs on package
and flat ODF export. Reuse PngImageWriter's size conversion for encoded
clipboard bitmaps, and libpng's chunk writer for native PNGs. Retain
compression, colour/unknown chunks and APNG frame data; leave PNGs with
physical metadata unchanged. Use actual pixel dimensions when preferred
pixel dimensions differ, and distinct bitmap containers for export-only
size changes so saving cannot alter the original graphic.

Preserve the appearance on the author display, including HiDPI, instead
of forcing 96 DPI. This cannot infer the unknown author DPI of old files
which have never been saved with resolution metadata. Other raster
formats and in-memory display changes are outside this change.

Cover six 96/144-DPI save/reopen variants, existing native metadata,
PNG byte/pixel/frame preservation, replacement and truncated input.

Assisted by GPT 6.1 Sol High

old_description:
wsl-as-helper: also look for ucrt64 in PATH to detect git-bash

*Issue*

When running wsl ./autogen.sh, we get the following error:

checking Visual C++... ./configure: line 14507: \Microsoft: command not found
./configure: line 14509: \Microsoft: command not found
checking VC++ Build Tools and similar... ./configure: line 14515: \Microsoft: command not found
configure: error: no Visual Studio 2022 installation found
Error running configure at ./autogen.sh line 338.

*Root cause*

The current version of Git for Windows (2.56) now ships
its runtime in a ucrt64 directory instead of mingw64, so the PATH
check used to detect the git-bash / wsl-as-helper method no longer
matches and the mode is silently disabled.

See https://lwn.net/Articles/1097213/

configure then fails with a confusing "\Microsoft: command not found"
and "no Visual Studio installation found", since the vswhere path ends
up built without the ProgramFiles(x86) prefix that only the wsl-as-helper
code path provides.

*Solution*

Look for ucrt64 in PATH as well in configure.ac and in the remaining
wsl-as-helper PATH checks in autogen.sh.

old_description:
tdf#173500 package: honor manifest.xml declarations for META-INF stream names

ZipPackageFolder::LookForUnexpectedODF12Streams rejected any stream
under META-INF/ other than manifest.xml or a name containing the
substring "signatures", even when the stream was explicitly declared
in META-INF/manifest.xml. Every other location checked by this
function already treats manifest.xml declaration as sufficient
grounds to accept an otherwise-unrecognized stream (see the
IsFromManifest() check a few lines below, for streams outside
META-INF); META-INF itself was the one exception, for no functional
reason found in the code or its history.

This made it impossible to embed any additional META-INF member -
for example a C2PA Manifest Store at the location required by the
C2PA specification, META-INF/content_credential.c2pa - in an
OpenDocument package without native rejection, even where the member
is declared in the manifest and even though ODF 1.3 Part 2, 2.2.2
(the "Extended Package" class) explicitly permits such members,
subject to the remaining ODF requirements.

Fix: also accept a META-INF stream when
ZipPackageStream::IsFromManifest() is true, matching the trust model
already used elsewhere in this same function. IsFromManifest() is set
while parsing META-INF/manifest.xml, before this check runs (see
ZipPackage::parseManifest), so this does not change the trust
boundary, only extends it consistently to META-INF.

Added a regression test (testMetaInfManifestDeclaredMember) with a
minimal ODT fixture containing one extra, manifest-declared META-INF
member with an unrelated name; loading must not throw ZipIOException.

old_description:
tdf#173562 shell: don't PropVariantClear an uninitialized PROPVARIANT

CPropertyHdl::LoadProperties declared a PROPVARIANT on the stack without
initialising it and called PropVariantClear on it as the first statement
of the loop. PropVariantClear dispatches on the .vt tag, so on the first
iteration it interpreted stale stack bytes: if they looked like VT_BSTR,
VT_LPWSTR or a vector type it freed a garbage pointer inside explorer.exe,
which is the STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION (0xc0000374) crash users see when
Explorer touches .ods/.odt files. The value loaded in the last iteration
was also never released.

Move the PropVariantClear to the end of the loop body: every clear now
sees the value that GetItemData / PSCoerceToCanonicalValue wrote in the
same iteration, and the last value is released as well.
new_description:
tdf#173562 shell: fix PropVariantClear on an uninitialized PROPVARIANT

CPropertyHdl::LoadProperties declared a PROPVARIANT without initialising it and called PropVariantClear on it. The PropVariantClear function frees the underlying elements of complex elements with known element pointers prior to freeing the containing element. If the stale stack bytes looked like a complex type it freed a garbage pointer inside explorer.exe, which causes the STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION (0xc0000374) crash.

Move the PropVariantClear to the end of the loop. Every clear now
sees the value that GetItemData wrote and the last value is released as well.

- found CPropertyHdl::LoadProperties and an odd looking PropVariantClear on first iterarion
- added an PropVariantInit and rebuild the propertyhdl.dll and debugged the result

tdf#173861 sc: support transposed vectors in FORECAST.LINEAR

Commit f336f63da900d76c2bf6e5690f1c8a7bd15a0aa2
(https://gerrit.libreoffice.org/c/core/+/20073) introduced
FORECAST.LINEAR and routed it through the same ScForecast()
implementation as ODF FORECAST. Its strict row/column equality check
therefore also rejects equal-length transposed vectors for the Excel
extension. ODF 1.3 Part 4 section 6.18.28 requires those constraints
for FORECAST, while FORECAST.LINEAR is a separate Microsoft extension.

Allow transposition only for the FORECAST.LINEAR opcode and only when
both arguments are one-dimensional vectors with transposed dimensions.
Read the second vector at swapped coordinates in both numerical passes,
keeping paired nonnumeric entries aligned. Preserve the strict ODF
FORECAST check and existing FORECAST.ETS dispatch.

Add a range-based regression for both matching and mixed orientations,
nonnumeric pairs, unequal lengths and the ODF shape guard. The matching
controls pass unpatched before a mixed case fails with Err:502; the
patched test passes. The full Calc core and statistical-function suites
pass, including the existing ETS fixtures. Recalculating the original
ODS also returns 1.5 for all four reported inline-array formulas.

Assisted by GPT 6.1 Sol High
new_description:
tdf#173861 sc: support transposed vectors in FORECAST.LINEAR

Commit f336f63da900d76c2bf6e5690f1c8a7bd15a0aa2
(https://gerrit.libreoffice.org/c/core/+/20073) introduced
FORECAST.LINEAR and routed it through the same ScForecast()
implementation as ODF FORECAST. Its strict row/column equality check
therefore also rejects equal-length transposed vectors for the Excel
extension. ODF 1.3 Part 4 section 6.18.28 requires those constraints
for FORECAST, while FORECAST.LINEAR is a separate Microsoft extension.

Allow transposition only for the FORECAST.LINEAR opcode and only when
both arguments are one-dimensional vectors with transposed dimensions.
Read the second vector at swapped coordinates in both numerical passes,
keeping paired nonnumeric entries aligned. Preserve the strict ODF
FORECAST check and existing FORECAST.ETS dispatch.

Add a range-based regression for both matching and mixed orientations,
nonnumeric pairs, unequal lengths and the ODF shape guard. The matching
controls pass unpatched before a mixed case fails with Err:502; the
patched test passes. The full Calc core and statistical-function suites
pass, including the existing ETS fixtures. Recalculating the original
ODS also returns 1.5 for all four reported inline-array formulas.

old_description:
tdf#163182: leave frame selection before hiding its text anchor

AI generated patch description: "With hidden characters shown, an image anchored to hidden text can be selected. Disabling hidden characters reformats its anchor out of the layout while Writer still treats the image as the selected frame. Layout and cursor updates then follow that selection and crash in SwAttrIter. The public ODT attached to this bug reproduces the crash on current Writer.

Before applying the view options, leave frame-selection mode in each synchronized view whose selected fly has a text anchor in hidden-character text that is about to be hidden. A fly anchored to visible text keeps its selection. The same handling applies to the toolbar command and direct UNO view-setting changes.

The regression test uses attachment 196746 for both entry points, with unselected and visible-frame controls.

Dependency: 212859 fixes an unrelated release-only Clang-plugin diagnostic on this base so the strict local build can run."

old_description:
desktop splash: Create splash screen instances directly, without UNO ctor

In order to create the splash screen instances used in
the Desktop class, no longer rely on the UNO service
constructors, but create instances of the corresponding
classes directly (UnxSplashScreen for the
"com.sun.star.office.PipeSplashScreen" service,
SplashScreen for the "com.sun.star.office.SplashScreen"
service).

Switch Desktop::m_rSplashScreen to a reference to
the more concrete SplashScreenBase base class instead of
one to the abstract css::task::XStatusIndicator UNO
interface (and rename the member).
This will allow further changes in the future
without being bound to specific UNO interfaces.

This requires linking the splash ("spl") library
into the desktop module. Make that conditional
on that library being built, using the same
condition as desktop/Module_desktop.mk
already uses to determine whether or not to build
Library_spl.

The now no longer needed UNO services and their ctors
will be dropped in an upcoming commit.

old_description:
tdf#158349 writerfilter: mv SdtPropertiesXMLs out of m_StreamStateStack

This should fix a (presumably minor) performance regression.

In an earlier 27.2 patch I moved SdtHelper into m_StreamStateStack.
(commit caa93e03abb4966d072af53208e81c41f2e3cb77)

But as vmiklos helpfully pointed out, one compontent of SdtHelper
was to parse and cache some separate xml files.
But now SdtHelper exists multiple times, so it potentially
is parsing/caching these xml files multiple times.

So move m_xPropertiesXMLs out of SdtHelper and (back) into
DomainMapper_Impl.
new_description:
tdf#158349 writerfilter: move PropertiesXMLs out of m_StreamStateStack

This should fix a (presumably minor) performance regression.

Earlier in 27.2 commit caa93e03abb4966d072af53208e81c41f2e3cb77
I moved SdtHelper into m_StreamStateStack,
and m_xPropertiesXMLs came with it
(although they aren't directly related).

As vmiklos helpfully pointed out, one compontent of SdtHelper
was to parse and cache some separate xml files like docProps/custom.xml.
But now SdtHelper exists multiple times, so it potentially
was parsing/caching these xml files multiple times.

So move m_xPropertiesXMLs out of SdtHelper and (back) into
DomainMapper_Impl.

old_description:
tdf#174076 sw: allow all use of table styles for insert/convert

Only the built-in table styles were being made available
for use when inserting a table, or converting text to table.

It was missing table styles that were imported with the document.

Ideally we could just use GetDoc()->GetTableStyles()
and forget about creating our own SwTableAutoFormatTable.
We probably could, but I just can't be confident that
in every conceivable case the SwDoc* will never be null.
So we add more wastefulness by copying it instead.

old_description:
gbuild: enable GDB's automatic symbol index cache

The Cppunit/Python debugger launchers and core-backtrace helper leave
GDB's index cache disabled by default. Repeated sessions can therefore
rebuild the same DWARF symbol index for large LibreOffice libraries.
Enable caching with -iex, before executable symbols are loaded, including
both coredumpctl routes. GDB manages the cache and keys entries by ELF
build ID. GDB_INDEX_CACHE=off disables this launcher default; a later
CPPUNITTRACE -iex command can also override it.

On Debian 13 arm64 with GDB 16.3, repeated loading and source lookup of
the matching 108 MB Debian LibreOffice 25.2.3 libmergedlo debug file took
median 5.01s uncached versus 1.65s cached. These are one-library symbol
lookup timings, not whole-application startup timings. Existing linker
.gdb_index support remains unchanged. The cache command requires GDB 8.3.

Validation used the actual expanded Cppunit and Python launcher blocks:
cache miss then hit, identical source/address locations, both opt-outs,
preserved inferior exit codes 0/7, environment and pretty-printer trust,
and unchanged LLDB/custom/no-trace command expansion. A generated real
core has identical registers and full backtraces with caching on/off.
Modern and legacy coredumpctl routing mocks also forwarded to real GDB.
Unwritable-cache and missing-build-ID execution controls pass. Shell
syntax and patch whitespace checks pass. Native macOS/Windows GDB and
an actual systemd coredump service were not exercised.

Assisted by GPT 6.1 Sol High

new_description:
gbuild: support opt-in GDB index caching for tests

Allow test and CI invocations to select a build-local GDB symbol index
cache without changing the account's GDB initialization file.
GDB_INDEX_CACHE=on enables caching in WORKDIR/gdbcache before loading
symbols; off disables caching. When unset, leave the user's enabled
state and cache directory untouched.

tdf#173626 Stop cycling through table style parents

AI generated patch description: "Some documents import a table style whose
parent resolves to the style itself. Editing Default Style makes
SwDoc::ResetTableStyles() walk each style's parent chain, so that self-parent
relationship hangs Writer. A cycle involving multiple styles has the same
failure.

Stop a parent walk when it revisits a style. An acyclic chain still visits the
same styles, and a descendant whose chain reaches the edited style is still
updated. Add a regression using the reported document, plus a two-style cycle
and the existing table-autoformat control.

The unbounded parent walk was introduced by 513bfbd476113f648090a8275cece4dc04ba0463.
The regression hangs without this guard and passes with it."

tdf#115747 Allow editing when lock-file creation fails

AI generated patch description: "A writable mounted Samba share can reject
LibreOffice's .~lock file while allowing document writes. Since
6ca3b3648e25ae9d4d2d29a0df83349198ec3f5e, this opens read-only to avoid
mistaking a failed lock creation for a corrupt lock file.

Offer Edit Without Lock only after primary lock creation fails and a direct
filesystem check confirms that no lock file exists. Opening read-only remains
the default. Ask separately before each unlocked save, since another editor's
changes may be overwritten. Do not claim ownership of a lock file after an
uncertain creation failure. Existing or corrupt locks, direct SMB/SFTP paths,
and unknown existence results retain their current handling.

The separate TempFileNextToLocalFile save behavior is unchanged. On a
macOS-mounted Samba share, the full edit/save workflow succeeded with that
existing setting disabled; same-directory saving failed on an unmodified
control share as well.

Focused sfx2 tests cover unattended opening, explicit edit consent, save
consent, and save cancellation."

Resolves: tdf#115747

old_description:
tdf#169429 md4c: preserve punctuation in Markdown autolinks

The permissive URL scanner excludes colon from paths and percent,
slash and semicolon from query strings. Consequently, the report's
bare URLs either lose their hyperlink completely or are linked only
up to the first semicolon; explicit Markdown links already work.

Allow those characters in their respective URL components. Keep
query semicolons as delimiters so sentence-ending semicolons stay
outside the hyperlink. Existing bracket and span boundaries remain
in place.

Add attachment-based checks for all four explicit/bare URL pairs,
plus coverage for trailing semicolons, surrounding parentheses and
emphasis. Both focused tests fail with the unpatched parser and pass
with the fix; the full Markdown suite passes. Reopening the original
attachment preserves all four complete hyperlink destinations.

Assisted by GPT 6.1 Sol High
new_description:
tdf#169429 md4c: preserve punctuation in Markdown autolinks

The bundled md4c scanner treats URI punctuation as word separators or
rejects it. Bare links therefore lose query semicolons or fail entirely
for paths containing colons, percent-encoded queries and redirect URLs.
Adding individual characters to the word allowlists still truncates
repeated semicolons and rejects adjacent colons or colons before slashes.

Scan the URL tail as a whole using URI punctuation, independently of
word-component separators. Keep the existing hostname and resolved-mark
checks, parentheses matching and Markdown/prose boundaries. Exclude
terminal sentence punctuation, including the existing semicolon boundary,
while allowing it internally. Email and explicit-link parsing stay separate.

Add the original attachment's four bare/explicit URL pairs and coverage
for repeated delimiters, redirect queries, fragments, ports, parentheses,
emphasis and terminal semicolons, periods and colons. This updates the
bundled md4c build; system-md4c builds need the corresponding library fix.

Assisted by GPT 6.1 Sol High

AI generated patch description: "The bundled md4c scanner splits or rejects punctuation in bare URL

authority port from the URL tail. Without that boundary, a nonnumeric

rejected nonnumeric port suffixes, localhost and email links. Writer's
explicit-link parser supplies independent destination controls for its
URL normalization. System-md4c builds require the corresponding fix in
the system library.

old_description:
tdf#163206 editeng: fix vertical misalignment when shrinking line spacing

In ImpEditEngine::CreateLines, when a proportional line-spacing rule below
100% (or the equivalent automatic content-scaling) shrinks the line height,
the max ascent was being recomputed from the unshrunken text height
(GetTxtHeight() * fSpacingFactor * ...). Because the max ascent defines the
text baseline position measured from the top of the line, the text was
drawn with its baseline too low in the shrunk line, leaving it off-center
relative to the bullet, the cursor, and the selection rectangle.

Fix by matching the baseline calculation that Writer already uses
(SwXTextDocument / itrform2.cxx), which sets the baseline to 80% of the
shrunk line height:

SwTwips nAsc = (4 * nLineHeight) / 5; // 80%

Compute the new line height first, then set the max ascent to 80% of that
height instead of the full text height, so the baseline stays centered in
the (shrunk) line.

tdf#163206 editeng: fix vertical misalignment when shrinking line spacing

drawn with its baseline too low in the shrunk line, leaving it off-center
relative to the bullet, the cursor, and the selection rectangle.

Update unit tests to take into account the new vertical line offset.

old_description:
chart2: free a partial wrapped-property map on allocation failure

AI generated patch description: "The property-map cache takes ownership
only after every entry has been inserted. If a map-node allocation
throws, the raw map and any adapters already moved into it leak. Failing
the first and second node allocations in LibreOffice's production
implementation reproduces both cases.

Own the map locally until it is complete. On an exception, release the
global osl mutex before destroying the partial map and remaining
adapters, whose destructors can release UNO references. Successful
construction and property lookup keep their existing behavior.

Port Collabora change 15938 to LibreOffice's global-mutex
implementation. A local ClearableMutexGuard replaces the fork's
caller-owned guard, so exception propagation requires no relocking. This
addresses an injected out-of-memory failure, not an observed ordinary
document-loading crash.

No unmerged prerequisite. Collabora change 15937 addresses a separate
callback-lifetime issue; combining the two must preserve this exception
cleanup."

Assisted by GPT 6.1 Sol High

old_description:
tdf#108638 vcl: retain fractional screen font sizes on Windows

Unverified Windows draft: no native Windows build or runtime is available
locally. Windows reproduction and before/after validation are required
before this proposal is ready for review or integration.

Windows shapes and draws screen text at rounded integer font heights,
while Calc maps cell widths continuously with zoom. This is the same
size-quantization mechanism reproduced on macOS and Linux for this bug;
the Windows report is not independently reproduced by this draft.

Reuse the per-font scale and GetScale dimensions for screen HarfBuzz
metrics, Windows Skia drawing and DirectWrite HDC drawing. Preserve the
height-relative stretch introduced by change 207990; it is not a proven
introducing change for this long-standing report.

Mark printer font faces during enumeration so the scale is immutable
from instance construction. Real printers have separate collections and
caches and retain integral GDI/HFONT sizing. Include temporary fonts.
Keep distinct fractional heights separate in the font cache.

Reuse the native zoom/cache regressions on Windows, selecting win/Skia
explicitly at 96 DPI. Cover two font families/sizes, twelve zooms,
both cache orders and compressed/expanded widths.

Remaining validation includes original attachments, raster/GPU drawing,
DPI, rotation/vertical text and printer/metafile controls. The legacy
ExtTextOut screen fallback still draws rounded HFONT outlines; handling
that mismatch requires Windows validation before promoting this draft.
Tiny-zoom bottom clipping is also outside this proposal.

Depends on 212151 PS4 for the per-font scale, not on Linux change 212207.
Host Clang plugin checks cover only shared sources' macOS branches;
they do not establish Windows compilation or a successful regression.

Assisted by GPT 6.1 Sol High

old_description:
tdf#108638 vcl: retain fractional font sizes in Linux GenericFont

Calc maps cell widths continuously with zoom, but GenericFont shapes
text at rounded integer pixel heights. Cairo draws at the same rounded
size, so the text width changes in steps relative to the cell width.
In attachment 134140, GTK3 consequently loses "example" from the first
line at 50% zoom and adds "to" at 40%, as described in comment 41.

Set the existing per-font scale in Linux GenericFont using the exact
selection height. Reuse GetScale for both Cairo and X11 Skia drawing
sizes, including the vertical font's swapped axes, so drawing, shaping,
metrics and outlines agree. Keep Fontconfig's rounded size selection
for hinting and bitmap strikes. QtFont keeps its default scale of one.
The font cache must distinguish exact heights in the same pixel bucket.

Extend the existing fractional-size regressions to Linux, covering
Liberation Sans/Serif, 10/12pt, twelve zooms, both cache lookup orders,
and compressed/expanded widths. The two regressions fail on the parent.
Original GTK3 document replays verify the 100/50/40% wrapping correction.
Tiny-zoom vertical clipping is a separate remaining symptom; this change
does not claim to fix the entire cross-platform report.

Depends on change 212151 for the per-backend font-scale mechanism.
Linux Cairo runtime tested: vcl_text 63, vcl_fontmetric 5 and
vcl_textlayout 3 pass. X11 Skia is syntax/plugin checked on the host;
no Linux Skia runtime or Windows coverage is claimed.

uitest: handle documents modified during close

CloseDoc synchronously when the model is still clean. A pending edit or
OnPrepareUnload listener can modify it after that check. PrepareClose()
then opens the save prompt while the test runner is blocked in the close
dispatch and cannot answer it.

The command-based shared-process path comes from
f5d97d14a2169c23b801d5d09ea19c001d36bba (Gerrit 149134). Dispatch close
asynchronously regardless of the earlier modified state, wait for either
a save prompt or view/document closure, and discard changes if prompted.
Keep the idle wait from 0deaf87f07a791eb7bc8f697863676b6677a9a6c
(Gerrit 194241), so Base closure finishes before the next document opens.
Report a timeout if the asynchronous dispatch produces neither event.

Add real UI tests for clean, already-modified and late-modified models.
The late case modifies the document from OnPrepareUnload, reproducing
the same blocked close branch without relying on scheduler timing.
The controls pass unpatched; the late case hangs at the save prompt.
With the fix, all three cases and the full demo_ui and math suites pass.

old_description:
tdf#173728 sw: discard RTF row backups after completing the row

A nested table's trowd can save its outer table's row definition. That
backup survived completed rows, so a later row without trowd restored
the obsolete definition instead of inheriting the preceding row.
This dropped cell contents and changed the table width, causing empty
cells and lost last-column character formatting in preceding rows.

Clear the backup after row processing, retaining recovery for resets
within the current row. Add reduced attachment-based regressions for
the missing final-row cells and last-column formatting/subscript.
Both tests fail without the fix and pass with it. Reopening the
original attachment also preserves the missing values and formatting.

Assisted by GPT 6.1 Sol High
new_description:
tdf#173728 sw: discard RTF row backups after completing the row

The report's bibisect identifies a regression from
d2e70beadd3392b0bf7b2f6e87edf23605575492 ("sw: RTF import: ignore
spurious table properties like Word, part 2"), reviewed at
https://gerrit.libreoffice.org/c/core/+/204407.

That refactor made restoreTableRowProperties() restore the complete
TableRowDef, including cell definitions. Previously recovery restored
row properties and the current cell position, leaving cell definitions
to the previous-row inheritance path when no cells were defined.

A nested table's trowd can save its outer table's row definition. That
backup survives completed rows, so a later row without trowd restores
the obsolete definition. Its nonempty cell list prevents inheritance
from the preceding row. In the attachment, an earlier two-cell row
replaces a four-cell row, dropping contents and changing the table width.
The width mismatch also causes empty cells and lost last-column
character formatting in preceding rows.

Clear the backup after row processing, retaining recovery for resets
within the current row and normal previous-row inheritance. The deferred
table-start handling and fresh trowd definitions from 204407 are retained.
Add reduced attachment-based regressions for the missing final-row
cells and last-column formatting/subscript. Both fail without the fix
and pass with it; reopening the original attachment also preserves
the missing values and formatting. The existing spurious-definition
tests testIgnoreTableDefinition and testIgnoreTableDefinitionBorders
pass in sw_rtfexport7, covering the behavior that 204407 intended to fix.

old_description:
tdf#161592 sc: avoid caching unfinished lookup results

A binary lookup into a long chain of dirty formulas can reach the
interpreter's recursion limit. InterpretTail then leaves the cell dirty

old_description:
tdf#173064 Fix Qt IME position after cursor changes

With the native Wayland input context, the candidate window can appear
at an outdated position after startup, a mouse click, or committed
input. Moving the cursor during composition can also reuse the old
preedit at the new position.

Commit any active composition before a mouse-driven cursor move, and
notify the Qt input method of the updated cursor rectangle after focus,
mouse handling, or committed input.
new_description:
tdf#173064 Notify Qt input method of cursor rectangle updates

Add a VCL-to-SalFrame notification for input method cursor rectangle
updates. Request updates when the caret geometry, coordinate mapping,
focus, or input window geometry changes.

In the Qt backend, defer and coalesce these requests so the input method
queries the rectangle after the updates have completed. Suppress requests
generated while answering a cursor rectangle query to avoid feedback loops.

Keep committing active composition before mouse-driven cursor moves
separate from cursor rectangle updates.

hyphenation points, which resulted in exceeding lines,

Regression since commit 391ea3bcb54698461bfb0f7be996cf95b91ebb0f
"tdf#170177 cui offapi sw xmloff: hyphenate at constituent boundaries".

old_description:
sc: clean up spelling edit view after switching documents

When a Calc spell dialog is closed after another document became active,
Reset() skips its view cleanup but still destroys mxEngine. The stored
EditView holds a raw pointer to that engine, so a later tiled paint reaches
EditView::SetBackgroundColor() through freed memory.

Remove the spelling view and kill its edit view before releasing mxEngine.
Also restore the document idle state that Init() disabled.

The LOK regression test opens the spell dialog, switches documents, closes
the first dialog, and paints the first document. It crashes at
EditEngine::SetBackgroundColor() without the cleanup.

Port of Collabora Online change I80e7021f59c47d2ab7f4e7622819dfa3245facf6:
https://gerrit.collaboraoffice.com/c/online/+/10059

old_description:
tdf#151802 sd: avoid duplicate master on slide paste

Copying a slide from the slide pane and pasting it back into the same deck
can add a fifth master page where the deck has four. The clipboard path first
imports the selected slide into a work document, then pastes that document
back. While matching the incoming layout, SdPage::Equals() rejects the
otherwise matching master: in the reproduced file, its Text Box 4 had
minimum text bounds 0x0 on the existing master and 15524x396 on the copied
master. The failed comparison renames the incoming layout, so later
master-page cleanup cannot recognize it as a duplicate.

EnhancedCustomShapeEngine::getTextBounds() returns an empty rectangle while
the shape is action locked. Custom shape geometry can be assigned after the
initial text-size calculation, leaving the minimum text bounds stale. Return
the calculated text bounds while locked and recalculate the minimum size when
the geometry item changes. The equivalent master pages then compare equal.

The bug report's bibisect points to Gerrit change 52526 (dfefe448), which
refactored getTextBounds() but retained the action-lock early return. The
lock check itself is older; this fix addresses the stale bounds and their
impact on the master-layout comparison.

Update the affected import reference dumps and turn the existing TDF#151802
FIXME into an assertion that the master count stays unchanged. This ports the
custom-shape part of Collabora change 11727; its separate OOXML group-import
and configuration-writer changes do not apply to this ODP reproduction.

Reproduced on macOS with attachment 183311 / sd/qa/unit/data/odp/tdf96708.odp
on base 63a2e191551b. testTdf96708 failed with 4 expected and 5 actual; with
this change it passes. CppunitTest_sd_uiimpress and CppunitTest_sd_import_tests
both pass; git diff --check passes.

Collabora change: https://gerrit.collaboraoffice.com/c/online/+/11727

old_description:
framework: avoid duplicate LibreOfficeKit status percentages

StatusIndicator::setValue sends a LibreOfficeKit callback when the integer
percentage is greater than or equal to the last one. Repeating the same
percentage does not report progress, but can invoke the client callback many
times during a long operation. Use a strict greater-than check to send only
actual increases.

Keep the monotonic behavior introduced by LibreOffice commit
ffa4b788191aa55d3ab57b499e89bb6cb56dbe6a (Gerrit 24326): it prevents a lower
percentage from making the progress bar jump backwards. Using != would allow
that regression; > preserves the guard and filters repeated percentages.

Collabora reports about 37,000 callbacks for roughly 100 distinct percentages
in one Calc load example. The local regression verifies the duplicate callback
sequence, but does not repeat that full-profile timing measurement.

Port of Collabora's fix:
https://gerrit.collaboraoffice.com/c/online/+/4658

old_description:
tdf#173259 sw: keep inline images in proportional line spacing

When proportional line spacing below 100% is applied to a paragraph with a
tall as-character image, Writer shrinks the whole line and forces its ascent
to 80%. The image height does not participate in the text spacing calculation,
so the image is shifted above its line and can be clipped in Writer and PDF.

For lines with a fly-content portion taller than the text, calculate the
spacing cut from the text height and take it off the line's top/ascent. Keep
the existing calculation for lines without such a portion. The regression
test covers a wrapped image, an image alone on a line, and an image sharing
a line with text.

This regressed with c012c74e69360dd78890c1d935b802c0baf79da2
(tdf#146081 sw: Fix inconsistent prop line spacing).

Port of Collabora's fix:
https://gerrit.collaboraoffice.com/c/online/+/10287

old_description:
vcl: own variations in PDF subset keys

Variable-font data used while emitting PDF subsets can outlive its
LogicalFontInstance. FontSubsetKey stays in the PDF writer's subset map
until emitFonts(), but it currently holds a reference to variations owned
by a LogicalFontInstance in a bounded cache. Cache eviction can release
the instance before PDF emission reads the key, leaving a dangling
reference.

Copy the variation vector into FontSubsetKey. The regression test releases
the font instance before checking the retained key. This lifetime problem
is relevant to the variable-font support added by TDF#171624
(https://gerrit.libreoffice.org/c/core/+/203243).

Port of Collabora's crashtesting fix by Caolán McNamara:
https://gerrit.collaboraoffice.com/c/online/+/5209

Assisted by GPT 6.1 Sol High

releases the font instance before checking the retained key. Its mock
font face reports that its tables are absent, allowing HarfBuzz to query
fvar without triggering the mock's unsupported-table assertion on some
platforms. This lifetime problem is relevant to the variable-font
support added by TDF#171624 and Gerrit change 203243.

new_description:
crashtesting: copy the variable font variations into the pdf subset key

crash on export sd-pol-tch-ar-886b709219d764a3.docx to pdf

FontSubsetKey held a reference to the variations owned by the font
instance. But the key stays in the subset map until the fonts are
emitted at the end of the pdf, while the instance lives in a bounded
least-recently-used cache and can be released before then.

Keep a copy of the variations in the key instead.

default stops from paragraph and paragraph style items. Those tab stop

Work on a copy and store the replacement back on the owning paragraph or
style. Only reformat when a replacement was stored. The regression test
retains the original pooled item and checks that the default change can be
undone and redone without changing that snapshot.
