sw: preserve wrap side for RTF drawing shapes

RTF \\shpwrkN selects both sides, left, right, or the largest side for text
wrapping. Writer kept this value for anchored pictures but sent it through
character properties when importing drawing shapes, so those shapes fell
back to two-sided wrapping and emitted an unhandled-token warning.

Keep the setting on RTFShape and map it to Writer's left, right, and dynamic
surround modes for drawing shapes. Continue to pass it to anchored-picture
wrap properties. Add regression fixtures for all three one-sided values.

On LibreOffice revision 72f02c674cd0dfd8a1e5b11ded9ed622502189e3, the new
left, right, and largest-side tests all returned PARALLEL instead of LEFT,
RIGHT, and DYNAMIC. The RTF importer files at that revision are identical to
the master base used for this patch. With the change, CppunitTest_sw_rtfimport
passes all 62 tests.

Port of Collabora Online change:
https://gerrit.collaboraoffice.com/c/online/+/12410
new_description:
sw: preserve wrap side for RTF drawing shapes

RTF \\shpwrkN selects two-sided, left, right, or largest-side text
wrapping. Writer kept this value for anchored pictures but routed it
through character properties for drawing shapes. Those shapes therefore
fell back to two-sided wrapping and emitted an unhandled-token warning.

Store the setting on RTFShape and map drawing shapes to Writer's left,
right, and dynamic surround modes. Retain the anchored-picture path. Add
fixtures for all three one-sided values.

On test base 72f02c674cd0, all three cases returned PARALLEL instead of
LEFT, RIGHT, and DYNAMIC. The importer files are unchanged on current
master. With the change, CppunitTest_sw_rtfimport passes all 62 tests.

Port of Collabora Online change:
https://gerrit.collaboraoffice.com/c/online/+/12410

old_description:
tdf#...... sc/searchresults: Show a separate string if no results found

If you search for a cell style and click “Find All” a dialog box will be
shown that lists all of the matches. At the bottom of the dialog is a
string saying how many matches there were. Normally it shouldn’t be
possible to have zero matches because the first dialog seems to only let
you select styles that exist in the document. However the second dialog
only actually lists non-empty cells, so it’s possible to make the dialog
appear with no matches by searching for a style that is only used by
empty cells. In that case the string would previously say “0 results”.

This patch changes the string to “No match found”. As well as probably
being more natural in English, this avoids a translation problem in a
few languages that treat zero as a singular number and then have
mistakenly hardcoded “one” in the translation. For example in the French
translation without the patch when there are no results it will say “une
correspondance trouvée”.

old_description:
Fix pretty-printer basegfx

The goal is to avoid infinite recursion when using
p <polygon var> in gdb.

For this, these changes were required:
For B2DPolygonPrinter and B2DPolyPolygonPrinter
- Avoid converting gdb.Value objects to strings to detect unavailable values,
it prevents from recursive pretty-printer invocations
- Check is_unavailable and is_optimized_out instead, preserving protection
against unavailable values and avoiding unnecessary calls into the inferior,
which can hang or fail when debugging core dumps

For B2DPolygonPrinter only:
- Make children() return an empty iterator when values are unavailable or memory access fails

Python Exception <class 'gdb.error'>: Error while looking for matching xmethod workers defined in Python.
Python Exception <class 'RecursionError'>: maximum recursion depth exceeded

which can be stopped only with several Ctrl-C

old_description:
NoOp sc: speed up Pearson and covariance matrix traversal

Retain one mdds storage position per operand for both statistical passes
instead of repeatedly searching for each cell's type and value. Follow
the iterator approach in EvalMatrix (93a779e56cc9cb02c0e053d7a58589ed9fd10636,
Gerrit 184358), using the existing position-aware accessors to preserve
encoded-error callbacks and operand error precedence.

Introduce a reusable paired numeric visitor with a focused contract test
covering storage order, booleans, text/empty exclusions, encoded errors,
zero values and empty matrices. Keep shape validation in the caller and
retain every Kahan update and the centered two-pass computation unchanged.

On an optimized Apple M3 Pro/macOS arm64 build, real interpreter timings
over precompiled tokens and existing matrices improve by about 51-55% for
larger numeric inputs and 79-81% for mixed text/blank inputs. PEARSON over
a 256x256 matrix drops from 2568 to 1218 microseconds per call. Eight
alternating process pairs, seven batches and nine inputs cover all seven
functions sharing this path (7056 checked batch measurements).

All 1570 numerical/type/error controls match before and after in result
type, error code and numeric bits. Calc core, formula2 and statistical
spreadsheet fixtures pass, as do actual compiler plugin checks. These
timings are local macOS evidence; no other platform speedup is claimed.

This is independently based on master and has no dependency on the
FORECAST proposals. No numerical behavior change is intended.

Assisted by GPT 6.1 Sol High

old_description:
ScriptForge Python iterable arguments

Before this patch:
calc.SetArray('A1', range(1, 11))
gaes an error, while
calc.SetArray('A1', tuple(range(1, 11)))
worked fine.

This is because Python objects that look
like a tuple or a list but are not
do not pass the Python->Basic bridge.

A Python tuple object, when populated
with scalar values, becomes easily
a Basic Array. A Python range object
has no equivalent in Basic.

The actual patch makes that all "iterable"
objects, like a range object, become
automatically tuples when they are used
as arguments in services methods.

Now,
calc.SetArray('A1', range(1, 11))
works fine too.

The user documentation should be updated
with a few examples showing this new option.

It is applicable only to Python scripts.

old_description:
tdf#173917: don't abort on macOS thread IDs larger than UINT32_MAX

sal/osl/unx/thread.cxx insertThreadId() aborted whenever
pthread_threadid_np() returned a thread ID that does not fit in
32 bits. Since macOS 27, the returned IDs exceed UINT32_MAX
(observed 7366983048 / 0x1b71b3d88 on the main thread), so
LibreOffice crashed with SIGABRT during InitVCL on every start.

Fold the 64-bit ID into the 32-bit oslThreadIdentifier instead
of aborting. The identifier is only used as an opaque per-thread
token, and for IDs that already fit in 32 bits the fold is a
no-op.
new_description:
tdf#173917: don't abort on macOS thread IDs larger than UINT32_MAX

sal/osl/unx/thread.cxx insertThreadId() aborted whenever
pthread_threadid_np() returned a thread ID that does not fit in
32 bits. Since macOS 27, the returned IDs exceed UINT32_MAX
(observed 7366983048 / 0x1b71b3d88 on the main thread), so
LibreOffice crashed with SIGABRT during InitVCL on every start.

Widen oslThreadIdentifier to sal_uInt64 on macOS and iOS so the
full 64-bit ID can be stored, and drop the abort. On other
platforms the type stays 32-bit. Adjust the two OpenGL debug
print statements that format the identifier accordingly.

Approach suggested by Patrick Luby in the Gerrit review of
Change 212152, who also verified that master builds and runs
with the widened type.

new_description:
tdf#173917: don't abort on macOS thread IDs larger than UINT32_MAX

On macOS 27, pthread_threadid_np() can return thread IDs larger
than UINT32_MAX, and insertThreadId() aborted on them, so
LibreOffice crashed on every startup.

The osl thread identifier does not have to be the OS thread ID;
it only has to be unique. Drop the MACOSX/IOS special case in
insertThreadId() so macOS and iOS use the same sequential
identifier counter as the other non-Linux platforms, instead of
storing the OS thread ID. This avoids the abort without changing
the public oslThreadIdentifier type, so the change can also be
backported to libreoffice-26-8 unchanged.

Approach suggested by Patrick Luby in the Gerrit review of
Change 212152, who also verified that it builds and runs
(main thread identifier 1, spellcheck thread identifier 13).
